title: OAuth 2.0 Token Revocation
subtitle: Signing out for real: the client tells the AS to invalidate a token, and the effect cascades to the whole token family (RFC 7009).

steps.label: Sign out / disconnect app
steps.lede: The user asks to end the session or disconnect the application. Nothing has hit the network yet.
steps.devtools: For a confidential (server-side) client the revocation call happens on your server — it will NOT show in the browser Network tab. Only a public SPA that revokes directly from the browser would be visible. Watch server / AS access logs otherwise.

steps.label: POST /revoke
steps.lede: The client sends the refresh token to the revocation endpoint, authenticating with its own client credentials. token_type_hint is just an optimization; if it is wrong the AS falls back to searching other token types.
steps.devtools: Filter for the /revoke path on as.example.com. The Basic value decodes to s6BhdRkqt3:cli-s3cr3t-shhh — which client is revoking. URL-decode the form body to read token and token_type_hint.

steps.label: 200 (empty body)
steps.lede: The AS verifies the client owns the token, invalidates it, and cascades to its dependent access tokens and — under rotation — the whole token family. Success is a bare 200.
steps.devtools: 200 + empty body = success — but 200 is ALSO returned for an unknown or already-invalid token (RFC 7009 §2.2). The endpoint is deliberately not a validity oracle, so the status tells you nothing about prior existence. The only meaningful error is 401 invalid_client (bad client auth); 400 unsupported_token_type if the type can't be revoked here.

steps.label: Discard local tokens
steps.lede: The client drops its cached access and refresh tokens and clears the local session. From the user's perspective they are now signed out.
steps.devtools: No network event. The local cleanup and the server-side revocation are independent — do both: clearing local storage without calling /revoke leaves a live refresh token on the AS.

steps.label: Next call with the revoked token → 401
steps.lede: The now-revoked access token (same family as the refresh token) is presented on the next API call. Because this resource server validates via introspection, it is rejected immediately.
steps.devtools: In the browser Network tab this is the visible effect of revocation: a 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token". Immediacy depends on validation: a resource server checking a self-contained JWT locally would keep honoring the token until its exp.

steps.label: How the API learns it's revoked
steps.lede: Behind that 401, the resource server introspected the token. After revocation the response flips to active:false — that flip is what produced the 401.
steps.devtools: Back-channel, not in the browser. Revoking the refresh token rt.8f3c1d9a-family-01 cascaded to the access token mF_9.B5f-4.1JqM in the same family. Confirm blast radius by introspecting a sibling access token — it too should read active:false.
